facts.text: Waterville was incorporated on June 23, 1802 after residents on the west side of the Kennebec River split from Winslow.
The city’s name comes from the original village called “Taconnet,” named after Chief Taconnet, located at the Kennebec and Sebasticook confluence.
In 1849 the Androscoggin and Kennebec Railroad opened to Waterville, later becoming part of Maine Central Railroad which built repair shops there in 1870.
Hathaway Company, a high‑end dress shirt maker that operated for over 160 years, was bought by Berkshire Hathaway and closed in Waterville.
The historic Hathaway Mill complex is now being redeveloped into mixed‑use space, including 65 affordable housing units funded by historic tax credits.
